facts.fact: Adwave's vendor page says its campaigns start from $30 a day across TV, Google Search, Facebook and Instagram.
facts.quote: Adwave starts from $30 a day across TV, Google Search, Facebook and Instagram.

facts.fact: According to Adwave's table, TikTok is an opt-in channel that starts at about $91 a day, and the user must turn it on and connect a TikTok account.
facts.quote: Opt-in from about $91/day; you turn it on and connect your TikTok account

facts.fact: Adwave's vendor page says its prepaid daily budget can be set from $30 to $10,000 a day, with no subscription and no contract.
facts.quote: you set anywhere from $30 to $10,000 a day, with no subscription and no contract.

facts.fact: Adwave's pricing page example shows a $75-a-day plan totaling $2,250 over 30 active days, which the article describes as a planning total.
facts.quote: a $75-a-day plan comes to $2,250 over 30 active days.

facts.fact: Adwave's vendor page says extra image creation costs $0.38 per image when ordered beyond the included campaign ads.
facts.quote: $0.38 per image, $6 per social video, $6 per 15-second TV spot and $12 per 30-second TV spot.

facts.fact: Adwave's vendor page lists TV, Google Search, Facebook and Instagram as running from the $30-per-day minimum.
Adwave's vendor page says the ads it creates for a campaign are included, and that new accounts start with an empty wallet that must be funded before launch.
facts.quote: The ads Adwave makes for your campaign are included.

facts.fact: Adwave's FAQ, as summarized on the vendor page, says card deposits carry a processing fee shown at checkout while ACH deposits do not.
facts.quote: card deposits add a processing fee shown at checkout and ACH deposits don’t.

facts.fact: The FTC Act's ban on unfair or deceptive practices covers online advertising, marketing and sales, according to FTC guidance cited on the page.
facts.quote: The FTC’s [guidance on digital advertising disclosures](https://www.ftc.gov/sites/default/files/attachments/press-releases/ftc-staff-revises-online-advertising-disclosure-guidelines/130312dotcomdisclosures.pdf) states that the FTC Act’s ban on unfair or deceptive practices covers online advertising, marketing and sales.

facts.fact: The page advises advertisers to avoid promising a specific bill reduction or payback period in an ad, because results depend on the home, roof, usage and utility rates.
facts.quote: Avoid promising a specific bill reduction or payback period in an ad, because results depend on the home, roof, usage and utility rates.

facts.fact: Required disclosures must be clear and conspicuous and placed close to the claim they qualify, and financing terms should not be hidden in fine print or on a separate page.
facts.quote: Required disclosures must be clear and conspicuous and placed close to the claim they qualify. Financing terms or assumptions should not be hidden in fine print or on a separate page.

facts.fact: Testimonials and endorsements fall under the FTC's Endorsement Guides, and a paid or rewarded customer or creator's relationship needs to be disclosed.
facts.quote: Testimonials and endorsements fall under the [FTC’s Endorsement Guides](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-16/chapter-I/subchapter-B/part-255).

facts.fact: Calling or texting leads requires proper consent under the Telephone Consumer Protection Act (TCPA), and the page calls purchased leads a real risk because some vendors cut corners on consent records.
facts.quote: Calling or texting leads requires proper consent under the [Telephone Consumer Protection Act](https://www.fcc.gov/sites/default/files/tcpa-rules.pdf) (TCPA).

facts.fact: One advertiser reported on Reddit's r/PPC spending about $2,000 on a solar video campaign that produced 3,000 clicks and no real leads, only fake form submissions.
facts.quote: One advertiser posted on [Reddit’s r/PPC](https://www.reddit.com/r/PPC/comments/16q84om/help_solar_lead_gen_campaign_3000_clicks_on/) about spending about $2,000 on a solar video campaign that produced 3,000 clicks and no real leads

facts.fact: Adwave reports last-touch credit and assisted conversions, supports Lift experiments, and the page says these attribution figures should be treated as estimates.
facts.quote: Adwave reports last-touch credit and assisted conversions and supports Lift experiments. Treat all of these as estimates
